author: OpenAI Codex assessment agent (thinker_assessments, contemporary follow-up)
changeNote: First complete 240-question assessment under the current 15 Values bank and scoring. Documented positions, user-authorised sound inferences and supported conditional neutral answers are distinguished. An independent evidence audit amended interpretation and source errors before archiving; substantive findings are recorded in review.notes. No 12Axes questions or scores were imported.

metadata.name: Anthony Albanese
metadata.description: Australian Labor prime minister combining public broadband and targeted industrial investment with tighter migration settings, expanded cash support, marriage equality and stronger defence capabilities through 2026.
metadata.period: 2022–4 October 2026; current government decisions weighted most heavily
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 2022–4 October 2026; current government decisions weighted most heavily. Coalition measures are attributed cautiously. Modern hypothetical policies are labelled inferred, not claimed as direct statements. Research cutoff 4 October 2026; later views do not overwrite a former governing period.

axes.brief: Electoral and parliamentary authority are central, with acceptance of the adverse Voice referendum result providing concrete accountability evidence.
axes.counterEvidence: Use of delegated migration rules does not itself establish a right to legislate contrary to Parliament or evade judicial review.

answers.rationale: His government seeks electoral mandates and accepts binding public votes, including the unsuccessful Voice referendum.
Expert advice informs cabinet proposals but does not replace elected authority.
His inclusion programme treats adult citizenship rather than education or intelligence as the basis of voting rights.
His policy changes proceed through parliamentary or legally delegated processes, not a claimed right to enact rejected statutes.
Opposition remains entitled to contest elections and challenge his programme.
Parliamentary scrutiny is compatible with his constitutional governing approach despite partisan conflict.
Constitutional courts constrain government, even where adverse decisions require revising policy.
Union participation in Labor does not replace general elections with union selection of the government.
Lawful opposition should compete; his hate-group restrictions concern defined extremist conduct rather than ordinary disagreement.

His acceptance of the Voice result supports binding constitutional referendums, while ordinary lawmaking remains parliamentary. A government-initiated constitutional vote is not evidence for a general voter power to repeal ordinary laws; the two institutional commitments support a mixed assessment.
Cabinet and parliamentary authorization constrain individual prime-ministerial policymaking.
Lawful parliamentary removal remains part of the accountability his institutional practice accepts.
Electoral timing must remain within constitutional authority rather than unilateral personal extension.
Voter accountability matters while representative terms and parliamentary confidence provide alternatives to automatic recall.
His constitutional programme does not justify authority beyond public scrutiny and removal.
Expanded defence capability remains subject to civilian democratic government.

axes.brief: Constitutional liberties coexist with strong safety, security, online and anti-hate regulation.
axes.counterEvidence: Expanded hate-group powers and restrictive firearm rules qualify a strongly libertarian interpretation; criticism alone is distinguished from threats.

answers.rationale: His health and policing approach retains restrictions on dangerous drugs despite recognising individual autonomy.
Judicially authorised surveillance can support serious investigations under legal safeguards.
Peaceful protest is legitimate while proportionate traffic and public-safety restrictions can remain.
Criticism should remain lawful when only offence is alleged, while threats and unlawful incitement are distinct harms.
Public-health regulation deserves weight, but protection from external harms differs from unlimited control over solely personal risk.
His AI privacy and safety approach weighs against routine universal tracking without suspicion, although security powers remain substantial.
Preventing impaired driving accords with his proportionate public-safety approach.
Independent court findings can justify narrowly limited restrictions on credible risks.
Expression deserves protection, but his anti-hate framework permits some limits where government identifies serious social harm.
Anonymous expression protects vulnerable participation while online safety and law enforcement may justify narrow identification duties.
Credible imminent violence can justify bounded searches, while antidiscrimination and legal safeguards constrain blanket powers.
Serious credible threats can justify preventative assembly restrictions with proportionate review.
Ordinary home entry should require lawful authorization, with urgent safety exceptions.
His September 2026 disclosure approach supports public accountability while retaining confidentiality for genuine national-security matters.
His government retains Australia's restrictive firearm framework, which does not generally recognise personal defence as a licensing reason.
Security detention should remain independently reviewable under his constitutional approach rather than solely executive discretion.

axes.brief: Multicultural inclusion and Indigenous recognition coexist with shared civic responsibilities and cohesion.
axes.counterEvidence: Social cohesion implies common institutions, not separate communities immune from shared civil law.

answers.rationale: His multicultural policy rejects automatic cultural hierarchy when harmless customs differ.
Multicultural grants and service training support practical public accommodation.
Common civic responsibilities matter without requiring newcomers to abandon inherited traditions.
Cultural heritage can coexist with full Australian civic participation.
Shared English access aids integration while multilingual public access also serves equal participation.
Indigenous acknowledgment and the Voice campaign support prominent recognition in public life.
Shared national traditions merit support without systematically excluding smaller communities.
His social-cohesion programme requires shared citizenship rather than separate identities overriding common public life.
A common holiday calendar can coexist with minority observance and accommodation.
His civic account includes Indigenous and immigrant traditions within national identity.
Social cohesion favours active participation in common institutions without cultural erasure.

His multicultural access and service-training programme supports additional languages on public signs where shared accessibility is preserved. This is an inference about public information rather than private commercial expression.
Families should not have to replace harmless inherited identity with a dominant cultural template.
Religious accommodation is reasonable where concrete identification and safety needs are satisfied.
His anti-racism and multicultural programmes treat plural backgrounds as legitimate parts of Australia.
Civic integration should not make cultural replacement its central objective.

axes.brief: Current September 2026 policy tightens temporary migration and removal while preserving skilled-family and humanitarian pathways.
axes.counterEvidence: The September 2026 package is a government announcement with regulatory implementation still relevant; it must not be confused with One Nation's more restrictive proposals.

answers.rationale: The government set a numerical Permanent Migration Program of 185,000 for 2025–26 and subsequently tightened visa settings. This supports qualified numerical control, although permanent-programme planning is not a fixed cap on every temporary arrival or on net migration.
Improved living conditions alone do not meet his government's selective admission requirements.
Skills and labour needs are prominent, though family and humanitarian routes remain important exceptions.
His government defends skilled migrants bringing families, while restricting some student-dependent routes.
Refugee protection should depend on need rather than cultural resemblance or labour-market usefulness, within managed pathways.
His current programme seeks stronger removal of visa overstayers rather than general permission to remain.
Migration targets and service capacity can justify limits despite employer demand.
His current effort to reduce net migration gives public-capacity pressure substantial weight.

Family places form part of the numerical Permanent Migration Program. This supports qualified inclusion in managed annual planning; restrictions on temporary students dependants alone would not establish the family-settlement proposition.
A job offer must meet visa, skill and other eligibility requirements rather than automatically justify admission.

Employer and family sponsorship are important channels, while independently assessed skilled and humanitarian pathways use different eligibility mechanisms. Family reunion is itself one of the sponsors in the statement, not an unsponsored exception.

The tightening of temporary visas and emphasis on skill and labour needs support requiring more than graduation alone for permanent settlement. This is qualified agreement: an educational credential can still help establish a route, and a route is not the same as automatic permanent status.
Humanitarian urgency may justify exceptions, while his government preserves managed resettlement and processing controls.
His multicultural equal-treatment framework rejects cultural resemblance as the general refugee-selection test.
Basic protection and lawful residency matter, while welfare eligibility can remain differentiated by status.
Diversity enriches national life but is not by itself a reason to expand numbers beyond family, protection and capacity considerations.

axes.brief: Growing defence investment and AUKUS coexist with diplomacy and regional cooperation.
axes.counterEvidence: Higher spending and long-range capabilities qualify peaceful rhetoric; professional forces and human-control concerns limit conscription and autonomous-weapons inferences.

answers.rationale: AUKUS and regional security commitments permit force beyond responding to an attack on Australian territory.
Diplomacy and regional engagement remain preferable where effective, alongside deterrence.
The 2026 defence expansion accepts substantial costs to strengthen capability, though this is framed as deterrence rather than unlimited dominance.
A credible imminent threat could justify prevention, while legality and escalation risks prevent a general pre-emption rule.

His February 2026 support for US action against Irans nuclear programme accepts preventive force in principle, but Australia restricted its own role to defensive support rather than joining the strikes. Endorsement of an ally and the rule governing Australias own use of force therefore pull in different directions.
His defence programme relies on professional capabilities rather than universal male conscription.
Negotiation can prevent war while major concessions that compromise security face limits.
His September 2026 insistence on human control over AI supports caution about autonomous lethal decisions despite defence technology investment.
Long-range maritime and allied capabilities go beyond simply repelling a territorial invasion.
Collective defence remains legitimate even when it entails military risk.
Submarine and regional capability investments support sustained operations beyond national territory.
Regional disputes should generally be managed diplomatically rather than escalated to war.
Credible deterrence can support bargaining without making coercion the preferred first instrument.
Avoiding escalation matters alongside the perceived need for credible strategic resolve.
Intelligence and cyber defence are important even where operations may strain diplomatic relations.
Verified reciprocal reductions can improve security without abandoning necessary deterrence.

axes.brief: Sovereign national decision-making coexists with alliances, trade rules and shared action on cross-border risks.
axes.counterEvidence: National migration control and domestic standards constrain unlimited supranational authority without negating cooperation.

answers.rationale: Sovereign national decisions remain important despite close alliances and shared rules.
Agreed international obligations can legitimately constrain some domestic choices.
Australian constitutional authority remains central to domestic legal interpretation.
AUKUS and the US alliance accept durable constraints in exchange for collective capability.
International membership rests on national consent, although treaty duties and consequences remain important.
International accountability is compatible with his rules-based diplomacy, subject to agreed jurisdiction.
National interests coexist with shared climate and security goals rather than invariably overriding them.

Climate and AI standards support coordinated action, while national implementation and sovereignty remain prominent. Common standards do not alone establish international authority to decide environmental policy; the appropriate transfer depends on the powers and accountability involved.

AUKUS and regional cooperation provide coordination while Australia retains its own foreign-policy decisions. Ordinary alliance membership does not establish support for a bloc requiring a common foreign policy, so cooperation and retained discretion support a conditional assessment.
Human-rights commitments can justify legal changes through domestic constitutional processes.
His economic programme retains an independent Australian currency.
Shared regional programmes can pool funding and decisions for common needs.
His current migration rhetoric emphasises sovereign admission control while retaining humanitarian cooperation.
Trading agreements can impose common rules where national labour and environmental protections remain viable.
Cooperation is preferred over absorption into a larger political federation.
Stable international rules require accepting some immediate domestic costs for durable cooperation.

axes.brief: Private enterprise coexists with explicit strategic public ownership, especially NBN, and mixed housing provision.
axes.counterEvidence: Community housing is not automatically state-owned. Public finance and incentives do not prove nationalisation of private providers.

answers.rationale: His business-investment programme retains a predominantly private economy alongside strategic public enterprises.
NBN ownership exemplifies a strong public role in essential network services.
Public accountability and universal access can favour public ownership beyond a narrow performance comparison.
Public investment vehicles and strategic alternatives can address market gaps without replacing ordinary enterprise.
Medicare and public hospitals support a substantial public delivery role alongside private providers.
His infrastructure approach supports continuing public control of core rail networks.
Lower cost can justify contracting, but public accountability and employment conditions must also be secured.
Public development finance can complement private banks in strategic and underserved areas.
Commercial holdings may be sold, but a continuing strategic public purpose weighs against automatic disposal.
Social housing expansion supports substantial public and community provision, while private rental supply remains central.
Regulated private ownership is acceptable in many strategic sectors where effective safeguards suffice.
His resource strategy uses private production, taxation and investment incentives rather than general nationalisation.
Private local-service contracts can work, while cost alone does not establish superiority over accountable public provision.
His explicit commitment to keep NBN public rejects selling strategic networks merely for revenue.
Losses warrant reform while universal-service obligations can justify continuing public ownership.
Public broadcasting is compatible with his multicultural and public-service approach rather than entirely commercial media provision.

axes.brief: Open trade is combined with selective industrial support and strategic investment screening.
axes.counterEvidence: Subsidies for emerging industry do not establish support for infant-industry import bans; the corresponding answer remains mixed.

answers.rationale: Trade access is valued, while selective industrial and security measures remain acceptable.
Competitive market access can outweigh some firm-level adjustment costs when workers receive support.
Domestic industry and procurement priorities can justify some preference over cheaper foreign bids.
Competitive imported inputs are valuable subject to security, labour and product standards.
Essential resilience matters, but domestic investment can be preferable to blanket restrictions on cheaper imports.
Negotiated liberalisation and reciprocity receive more weight than an unconditional unilateral rule.
Industrial subsidies support emerging sectors, but that does not itself imply restricting competing imports and raising consumer prices.
Foreign business investment is welcome with security screening, although established-home purchases face a distinct restriction.
Farming resilience matters while agricultural exports and affordable inputs favour open trade.
Adjustment and productivity investment are ordinarily preferable to permanent protection for every domestic producer.
Retaliatory tariff escalation can harm an export-oriented economy; negotiation and diversification are more consistent first responses.
Equal product taxation fits fair competition apart from specific lawful trade remedies.
Demonstrable foreign subsidisation can justify proportionate remedies where domestic competition is materially distorted.
Tariff-reducing agreements can increase prosperity while resilience safeguards manage dependency.
Strategic security can justify blocking particular foreign takeovers despite larger investment offers.
Foreign online services should generally remain accessible under common safety and consumer rules rather than special nationality barriers.

axes.brief: Markets allocate ordinary production while national industrial strategy, subsidies and wage rules shape development.
axes.counterEvidence: Regulated private-currency competition is distinct from abolishing public money. Planning does not extend to normal output quotas across the economy.

answers.rationale: His startup and business-tax measures leave ordinary production decisions with firms.
Industrial targets and subsidies do not establish compulsory output quotas across important sectors.
Market prices remain normal while specific essential-service affordability problems justify intervention.
National reconstruction and industrial policy deliberately steer investment into selected strategic sectors.
Consumer demand generally guides expansion and closure, qualified by strategic resilience and labour protections.
Energy and essential-service affordability can justify targeted government price constraints.
Startup incentives support market entry without requiring official proof that additional output is needed.
Public investment vehicles steer some finance, but this does not imply directing all private banks' ordinary lending.
Open capital movement supports investment, subject to sanctions, tax compliance and security safeguards.
Selected industry support is a deliberate instrument even when immediate private returns favour other sectors.
Regulated private payment innovation can coexist with official money, while monetary stability and consumer risk constrain broad currency competition.
His wage policy supports a legal minimum rather than relying entirely on unequal individual bargaining.
Collective bargaining remains important alongside minimum wages and award protections rather than comprehensive government wage schedules.
Central-bank independence is more consistent with his framework than direct cabinet control of lending and interest rates.
His housing policy emphasises supply and assistance rather than general rent freezes, while limiting increase frequency and strengthening tenancy rights.
Strategic national investment does not normally replace firms' production and distribution decisions across the economy.

axes.brief: Cash-support increases and progressive asset-income reform coexist with worker tax cuts, investment incentives and fiscal limits.
axes.counterEvidence: Work obligations and movement between payments are not complete expiry of support. Capital-gains and trust-income taxation are not a general net-wealth levy.

answers.rationale: Progressive tax reform and cash support seek to reduce material disadvantage while retaining incentives to invest.
Fairness can justify narrowing gaps, while his reform also emphasises aspiration, investment and letting workers keep more income.

Higher parenting payments, rent assistance and JobSeeker strengthen cash support. The April 2026 government report records increased payment rates and safety-net investment, supporting a stronger income floor with fiscal limits rather than relying on Medicare as income evidence.
He improves benefits beyond subsistence but does not seek to erase most differences in living standards.
Progressive contribution and the 2026 trust and capital-gains proposals give affluent income recipients greater obligations.
Worker tax relief supports retaining earnings while targeted higher contributions from asset income reduce unequal treatment.
His current tax reforms concern capital gains and trusts rather than a general large-inheritance levy.
Continued means-tested support and extended parenting eligibility differ from cutting all support after a fixed duration while need persists.
Asset-income reform increases contributions associated with wealth, but differs from taxing accumulated net wealth to fund cash transfers.
Modest increases coexist with fiscal restraint; lower taxes are not the sole reason to hold benefits down.
His security and inclusion rationale supports enough cash for participation, although actual benefit adequacy remains contested.
Worker tax cuts and increased targeted payments both receive priority, preventing an unconditional tax-first rule.
Family and rent assistance can supplement low earnings, alongside tax offsets that reduce rather than necessarily refund liability.
Progressive marginal rates remain central rather than an identical additional-income tax rate for everyone.
Housing supply, assistance and tax reform are preferred to broad compensated redistribution of large landholdings.
Support for eligible working families and renters extends beyond households already unable to meet basic survival needs.

axes.brief: Civil authority and plural religious citizenship coexist with faith-community consultation and public service partnerships.
axes.counterEvidence: Personal Catholic identity is not used as evidence of clerical lawmaking or religious family courts.

answers.rationale: Equal citizenship and plural faith protections favour publicly defensible laws rather than reliance on one religion.
Religious values can inform citizens without being an official binding source of legislation.
Civil government does not require clergy to approve its policies.
His multicultural equal-treatment approach weighs against founding the constitution on one selected religion.
Neutral religious literacy supports understanding while public schools should not recruit pupils into a faith.
A state-faith curriculum conflicts with plural citizenship even where voluntary faith education receives support.
Civil institutions determine enforceable law rather than clerical rulings.
Consultation with faith leaders does not imply a privileged official role in reviewing all proposed laws.
Inclusive religious ceremony can have civic meaning, while compulsory worship would exclude nonbelievers.
Faith-school and community support may have public purposes, but strengthening belief itself requires distinct justification.
Familiar symbols may remain historical features, while official endorsement implying unequal citizenship should be constrained.
Shared festivals can remain holidays, but explicit state recognition of a predominant faith sits uneasily with equal religious citizenship.
Clerical office alone should not confer a seat in government.
Cooperative religious arrangements may justify some recognition, while equal treatment limits exemptions beyond comparable charitable work.
Civil marriage should remain independent of religious permission.
Religious mediation can be voluntary, but legally binding family decisions must preserve civil rights and judicial safeguards.

axes.brief: Gender equality and diverse family recognition support social reform without requiring every voluntary tradition to disappear.
axes.counterEvidence: Social recognition questions are inferred from family and equality policies rather than treated as identical to formal legal eligibility.

answers.rationale: His equality programme supports substantial changes to exclusionary inherited customs.
Tradition has value but does not automatically outweigh contemporary equality.
Expanded single-parent support and inclusive family policy reject privileging only married two-parent households in social recognition.
His gender programme challenges fixed traditional roles and barriers to women's participation.
His established marriage-equality position supports marriage regardless of sex.
Family stability matters without making one married household form socially superior to other caring families.
His women's-health and autonomy orientation supports social acceptance of early abortion, with medical safeguards.
Families deserve involvement while public education has duties beyond preserving every parental sexual norm.
Equal family recognition supports accepting same-sex adoptive parents under ordinary child-welfare standards.
Public dress should principally reflect personal choice rather than uniform inherited modesty expectations.
Respect for identity supports inclusive language while questions of legal compulsion remain separate.
Established customs should not automatically prevail when they perpetuate exclusion.
Equal acceptance should extend beyond traditional sex-role expectations.
Consensus and orderly implementation matter, while urgent equality concerns can justify faster reform.
Inclusive teaching should explain varied orientations and identities in age-appropriate ways despite some traditional objections.
Heritage can be meaningful voluntarily without obliging society to preserve every obsolete custom.

axes.brief: Current AI investment and faster development are paired with enforceable standards and stronger concern about loss of human control.
axes.counterEvidence: July 2026 AI standards were proposed for later legislation; September safeguards do not equal a general technology moratorium. Speculative biomedical answers remain explicit inferences.

answers.rationale: His 2026 AI framework seeks substantial deployment and investment despite uncertainty, conditioned on enforceable safeguards.
His framework supports staged testing where needed but not a blanket restriction of every new technology to small trials.
Accelerated housing and infrastructure delivery can justify some permanent habitat loss when assessed benefits and safeguards warrant it.
Strong medical evidence remains necessary before widespread use, with proportionate pathways for urgent needs.
Productivity gains and investment are welcomed, while worker conditions and retraining require protection.
Environmental standards matter, while major housing and infrastructure needs prevent automatic preservation priority.
Food innovation can support climate and productivity goals with regulatory assessment even before every long-term ecological effect is settled.
Invasive enhancement in healthy people warrants research restrictions until strong long-term safety evidence exists.
His industrial decarbonisation strategy gives technological solutions substantial priority, while retaining efficiency and emissions constraints.

His development programme seeks timely environmental assessment while requiring safeguards for serious harms. A project with poorly understood substantial effects may merit delay, but risk severity and mitigation affect that decision; the question does not imply indefinite postponement.
Adult autonomy matters, but basic initial safety alone does not resolve invasive-device long-term risks.
His AI safety and health focus implies supervised diagnostic deployment until reliability across groups is demonstrated.
Irreversible heritable enhancement raises ethical and safety risks beyond ordinary innovation incentives.
Agricultural productivity and ecological protection warrant proportionate long-term evidence without assuming either automatic clearance or blanket prohibition.
His current housing-supply and infrastructure programme gives development substantial priority in direct conflicts, subject to environmental safeguards.
His September 2026 demand for human control and guardrails supports delaying potentially irreversible harm until strong low-risk evidence exists.

axes.brief: National social and economic standards coexist with federal states and locally informed implementation.
axes.counterEvidence: A national Indigenous advisory Voice did not itself create autonomous territorial governments; local-governance support is therefore moderate.

answers.rationale: States retain constitutionally protected powers despite national policy disagreement.
Federal and state authority are constitutionally distributed rather than decided solely by national preference.
His federation provides no automatic unilateral regional secession right by simple majority vote.
Legitimate national programmes can justify overriding obstructive regional measures within constitutional powers.
State constitutions are compatible with the national constitutional order.
National policing addresses federal functions while ordinary policing remains substantially state-based.
National equalisation and service financing weigh against regions keeping most receipts regardless of need elsewhere.
Common national educational standards receive weight while states retain implementation and curriculum responsibilities.
Regional tax differences remain legitimate within constitutional and intergovernmental limits.
Common national employment protections prevent inconsistent basic labour standards across regions.
Local institutional changes ordinarily need no Commonwealth approval, while state law and rights remain relevant.
Medicare and national service guarantees support common covered-care standards alongside state delivery.

The Voice proposal sought representation and advice rather than independent authority over land and education. Support for community input favours local influence, while retaining ordinary legislative responsibility limits the stronger autonomy mechanism in this question.
National fiscal coordination can limit damaging regional tax competition.
Region-confined land and wildlife decisions ordinarily warrant regional control within protected rights.
Multi-region disasters justify national coordination and direction, qualified by operational state responsibilities and local knowledge.

axes.brief: Social opportunity, gender barriers and learned prejudice receive causal weight while individual traits retain mixed biological and environmental explanations.
axes.counterEvidence: Causal judgments are not scientific findings attributed to Albanese. National-IQ, racial violence and self-control answers use modest inference strength and mixed personal-trait answers.

answers.rationale: His education, childcare and opportunity approach assigns substantial formative weight to social surroundings.
His investment in educational opportunity makes social explanations more plausible than inherited national IQ hierarchy; this remains a modest causal inference.
His women's-equality speech explicitly identifies social barriers and expectations as shaping participation and outcomes.
Biological sensitivity and unequal exposure both affect stress; his health and social policies address interacting causes.
Training, access and opportunity are intended to alter interests and life chances through experience.
His innovation policy recognises risk-taking responses to incentives while individual disposition can also matter.
His social-cohesion training assumes cooperative habits can be cultivated through shared civic experience.
Empathy can involve dispositions and learning; his representative-government argument gives experience a substantial role.
Early education and developmental support assume surroundings can improve attention and learning.
Moral reactions can reflect both dispositions and learned norms; equality principles alone do not establish biological predominance.
Anti-prejudice education assumes perceived threat can be learned through social exposure and changed through knowledge.
Biology can contribute to temperament while developmental surroundings remain consequential; neither universally dominates.
His emphasis on cultural representation and social expectations makes learned attractiveness preferences a plausible moderate inference.
His account of Indigenous disadvantage and opportunity favours social explanations rather than biological racial violence, without claiming scientific proof from policy.
His investment in learning and social opportunity supports learned self-control over inherited racial tendencies as a modest inference.
His 2026 speech directly attributes improved gender outcomes to reforms and barriers, contradicting an explanation based simply on different economic value.

review.notes: Independently reviewed all 240 exact statements with current 2026 primary evidence, including September AI remarks, migration settings and April cash-benefit reporting. Clarified permanent-programme numerical planning versus a universal arrival cap, family sponsorship versus unsponsored humanitarian routes, and graduate pathways versus automatic residency. Corrected coordinated standards versus transferred environmental authority, alliances versus compulsory common foreign policy, and Voice advice versus independent territorial authority. Balanced support for preventive US Iran strikes against Australias own defensive-only role instead of inferring a use-of-force rule from alliance membership. Added direct cash-support evidence, preserved the distinction between work conditions and complete benefit expiry, and repaired delay rhetoric that overstated the environmental question. Neutral answers identify competing commitments, with hypothetical technology and human-trait judgments explicitly inferential. No distribution or similarity tuning; batch similarity and portrait validation remain separate. Independent close-neighbour review on 2026-10-04 compared exact answers, periods and policy mechanisms with julia-gillard revision 1. Specific corrections and retention reasons are recorded in review.similarity; no score tuning was used. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers.

similarity.reason: Retain both revision 1 profiles after independent exact-question comparison. Gillard is confined to 2010–2013 minority-government conduct; Albanese is assessed through 4 October 2026, with current policies weighted. Both retain Labor mixed-economy, welfare, federal and alliance commitments, so close aggregate scores are expected. Their records sharply diverge on the exact marriage question (Gillard’s in-office opposition versus Albanese’s support). Gillard transferred some single parents to lower Newstart payments; Albanese expanded parenting eligibility and increased JobSeeker and rent assistance. Her carbon-price mechanism and national school agenda differ from his current industrial-investment, faster housing-development and migration-reduction priorities. Relevant item distinctions include progressive05, redistribution03/11, planning04/10, immigration08 and innovation15. Pair review corrected residual cash-versus-services rationales, subsidies-versus-import-restrictions, and constitutional-referendum-versus-ordinary-law-repeal reasoning, even though these corrections may increase aggregate resemblance. Distinct periods, policy mechanisms and opposite marriage positions warrant retaining both; scores were not tuned to clear the warning.
